errors.english: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
errors.why: The objection is that recognition and the parts produce the cognition OF the whole; the whole is the object of the cognition, not its producer.

fix.find: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
fix.replace: The text states that [recognition and the parts] produce the cognition of the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin), the whole composed of parts.

errors.english: then the valid means of knowledge would be consistent with the object.
errors.why: དོན་དང་ལྡན་པ here is arthavat, 'purposeful/meaningful': if certainty came only from pramāṇa, pramāṇa would have a point.

errors.english: the inference that determines the other parts is a sign established by direct perception.
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of a sign whose RELATION (འབྲེལ་པ) is established by perception, and the inference arises from that sign (continuing on the next side); the inference is not itself the sign.

note: Generally follows the Pramāṇa commentary on the avayavin, but misreads who produces the cognition of the whole and loses the 'relation' in the closing argument.
A careful lemma-by-lemma rendering of a terse commentary on cowness and universals; the dialectical moves are correctly assigned.

errors.why: ཡིད་གཅུགས་ means 'trusting, confident' (viśvasta), as the gloss 'without suspicion' confirms, not 'affectionate'.

note: Faithful rendering of the word-glosses on the tigress episode.
Accurate Vinaya rendering of the end of the first saṃghāvaśeṣa analysis and the stages of emission, with correct offense terminology.

errors.english: These phenomena are neither with affliction nor without affliction.
errors.why: The sūtra says these dharmas are without affliction; they are not accompanied by affliction, so 'neither... nor without affliction' denies what the text asserts.

fix.find: These phenomena are neither with affliction nor without affliction.
fix.replace: These phenomena are without affliction; they are not accompanied by affliction.

errors.english: Once he knows the source of all phenomena
errors.why: འབྱུང་བ here continues the preceding 'emergence' (niḥsaraṇa): he knows all dharmas as emergence/deliverance, not their 'source'.

note: Good rendering of the Madhyamaka argument and the Akṣayamati quotation, except one reversed statement about affliction.

errors.why: This is the commentator's abbreviation instruction, 'supply [the rest] likewise', not a statement about composition.

fix.replace: [The rest is to be supplied in the same way.]

note: Readable rendering of the abridged Sadāprarudita episode; one abbreviation formula is mistranslated and the closing sentence is loosely restructured.

errors.english: By these words, the lord of men
errors.why: Completing མ་བཀུར་ from the previous side (Skt. vimānena), it says 'by that disrespect' the king was left downcast, not 'by these words'.

errors.english: Who are victorious and adorned with the beauty of supreme things—
errors.why: 'Those victorious ones' are the worshippers of the Jina, whose commands even the gods bear on their heads; the English makes the gods the victorious ones.

note: Fluent verse rendering of the Tibetan; the transliterated Sanskrit is correctly left as notes, with two misread referents.
Accurate rendering of the momentariness argument, including the variant reading and the siddhāntin/opponent turns.

errors.english: by using factors that are not incompatible with the body and the mind of an omniscient one
errors.why: The Mīmāṃsakas use body, mind and the like, which are NOT incompatible with omniscience, to deny an omniscient being; body and mind are the reasons, not what they are compatible with.

fix.find: by using factors that are not incompatible with the body and the mind of an omniscient one
fix.replace: by means of body, mind and the like, which are not incompatible with omniscience and so forth

errors.english: the object to be negated by the cognition and its object is existing because it is designated as existing, and their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception
errors.why: The cognition and its object are themselves what is called the existence of the thing to be negated, and their absence is the non-existence that consists in non-perception; the cognition does not negate anything here.

errors.english: conditioned by the blessing [note: or influence]
errors.why: In this causal-efficacy argument བྱིན་གྱི་རླབས་ is a modifying influence on the cause, not a 'blessing'.

note: Follows the anupalabdhi discussion broadly but garbles two key arguments, including the anti-Mīmāṃsaka point about omniscience.

errors.why: The subject is Moon (ཟླ་བ), who speaks; the youths reply in the next sentence.

errors.english: one line of text regarding the King's reaction
errors.why: A stray editorial fragment with no counterpart in the Tibetan is appended to the sentence.

fix.find: one line of text regarding the King's reaction

errors.english: Moon must be separated from his captivating mind
errors.why: ཡིད་འཕྲོག ('captivating') qualifies Moon or names what he is to be parted from; 'his captivating mind' is not in the Tibetan.

errors.english: He possessed noble qualities and fine intelligence, becoming a worthy object of great praise.
errors.why: This opens a verse (with the following lines on lineage and the dog/oyster simile) but is merged into the prose narrative.

note: The narrative is broadly followed, but there is a wrong speaker, a stray editorial fragment at the end, and a verse folded into prose.
